Lessons.Title: Residuals
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: define a residual as observed output minus predicted output; calculate and plot residuals; explain patterns or systematic errors indicating that a linear model is or is not appropriate. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 3 Lesson 6, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/3/6/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). The teacher and student source emphasize connecting points to residual graphs and interpreting model fit, not merely evaluating isolated subtraction.

Original dataset of hypothetical machine readings: paired (x,y)=(0,2),(1,4),(2,7),(3,9), with fitted line y=2.4x+1.9 from the prior learning sequence. Predicted outputs 1.9,4.3,6.7,9.1 yield residuals +0.1,-0.3,+0.3,-0.1. These residuals sum to zero and have squared sum 0.20; the horizontal residual axis is y=0, not the original regression line.

Original contrasting example for detecting curvature: x=−2,−1,0,1,2 and y=4,1,0,1,4. The horizontal line y=2 predicts the same number for every x. Residuals are 2,−1,−2,−1,2, a curved U pattern rather than apparently random scatter. A trend in residuals signals that a straight-line model leaves structure unexplained. The teacher must evaluate whether a model and its domain are meaningful.

Student activity: create an accessible two-column observed/predicted table, sketch a signed residual plot, compare a roughly unpatterned sequence against a visibly curved one, and critique an incorrect residual obtained by subtracting in reverse order. Disclose when plots are manually constructed instead of using actual software.

Teacher-scored rubric: 0–2 each for correct predicted values, signed residuals and zero-axis plot, reasoned pattern-based model critique, and appropriate contextual/technology limits (maximum 8). An automatically graded residual number alone does not demonstrate the source plotting and critique tasks.

KeyConcepts.Title: Residual
KeyConcepts.Definition: The vertical difference from a measured response to its model prediction.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Residual = observed y minus predicted ŷ; preserve sign.
KeyConcepts.Example: At x=1, y=4 and ŷ=4.3 produce residual −0.3.

KeyConcepts.Title: Residual plot
KeyConcepts.Definition: A graph of residuals against explanatory x-values.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Plot residuals above or below a zero horizontal axis, with consistent scale.

KeyConcepts.Title: Residual pattern
KeyConcepts.Definition: Structured curvature in residuals indicates the linear model may not capture a nonlinear trend.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Inspect shape and scatter, not only sum of residuals.
KeyConcepts.Example: For y=x² at x=−2,...,2, residuals against line y=2 show U-shape.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find signed residuals
WorkedExamples.Question: Use the fitted line y=2.4x+1.9 for measured y=2,4,7,9 at x=0,1,2,3.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the exact first-party paired-data model, compute each quantity, and interpret mathematical evidence.
Steps: Subtract predicted from observed in matching rows: 2−1.9=+0.1; 4−4.3=−0.3.
WorkedExamples.Check: Each residual equals its actual minus model prediction.

WorkedExamples.Title: Distinguish the residual axis
WorkedExamples.Question: Where would the residual for x=1 be plotted?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the exact first-party paired-data model, compute each quantity, and interpret mathematical evidence.
Steps: Place a dot at (1,−0.3) on axes x versus residual, below y=0.
WorkedExamples.Check: A negative residual means the observation lies below the model.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find curvature in a residual graph
WorkedExamples.Question: For y=x² at x=−2,−1,0,1,2, evaluate residuals relative to model ŷ=2.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the exact first-party paired-data model, compute each quantity, and interpret mathematical evidence.
Steps: Arrange in x order to observe high positive tails with a negative center.
This U-shaped pattern suggests a constant/linear model misses important curvature.
WorkedExamples.Check: Residuals exhibit symmetry and systematic curvature, not random scatter.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: This reverses residual signs and wrongly places points.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use observed minus predicted every time.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Concluding a model is good because residuals sum to zero
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A fitted linear model with intercept can have zero residual sum yet still show curvature.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Plotting residuals on the original y-axis without zero baseline
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The residual chart measures error, not measured outcome.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Label residual units and draw zero line.

SummaryPoints: Residual = observed response − model prediction and may be positive or negative.
A residual plot is interpreted relative to y=0.
Nonrandom patterns can reveal inadequacy of linear fit even when residuals sum to zero.
Teacher reviews plotted structure and critique; static examples are not proof of software use.

Visuals.Title: Accessible original bivariate statistical calculations
Visuals.Description: Original invented observations with explicit signs and labels; these are not actual classroom measurements.
